goldens.comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
goldens.reasoning: None of the candidates mentions the recursive call to session.identityProviders().getById() in getForLogin.

goldens.comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same bug: cleanup removes the literal 'alias' instead of the IDP that was just created.

candidates: Cleanup is removing the literal alias 'alias' instead of the IDP that was just created, so created IDPs are not cleaned up and cleanup may fail if no IDP with alias 'alias' exists

remove(alias) only invalidates the IDP's internalId cache when the alias cache entry exists or is marked invalid - if alias entry isn't cached, CachedIdentityProvider is null and no invalidation occurs, leaving potentially-stale internalId cache entry
In remove(alias), if the alias doesn't exist and the alias key is invalidated, registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) can throw NPE

Login cache stores results for each distinct organizationId inside a single IdentityProviderListQuery keyed only by (realm, fetchMode), which can grow the searchKeys map without bound in realms with many organizations, increasing memory pressure and replication costs
